_comment: Invrisil 8c Task C1 (issue #12) -- ~14x10 Brothers' parlor (hideout interior, 'borrowed elegance': shabby-genteel, one absurdly good rug, warm low light over the card table). biome brothers_parlor (see biomes.json's own _comment for the already-present-asset picks). entities._comment: Round-trip pair with alleys_to_parlor (mercantile_alleys cell 19,12). This is the parlor's ONLY exit -- a dead-end hideout interior, matching witch_hollow's own single-purpose-room shape one map further in.

Invrisil 8c Task C1 (cast) + Task C3 issue #13 (this edit -- wires `conversation`) -- Wilovan, CANON (wiki.wanderinginn.com/Wilovan, WIKI-VERIFIED 2026-07-08, same verification C2's combatant record already banked): a Gnoll [Thug] of the Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings, brick-built, dapper vest/leggings/tall hat, gentlemanly courtesy -- 'perfect gentlemen. Until the hats come off.' The plan's User-ratified shape 1 (WILOVAN fronts the Brothers, supersedes the dialogue-drafts lane's ORIGINAL 'Mister Sable' -- that draft's register informs a background Brother, never fronts). The commission/ways/marker quest graph (data/dialogue/invrisil_wilovan.json, recast Sable->Wilovan from docs/design/dialogue-drafts/invrisil/brothers_lieutenant.json) now lands -- talk_pool stays the pool-then-conversation precedent's first-talk-of-a-waking flavor (interact()'s npc branch), `conversation` carries every later talk into the real graph. Sprite: reused `pc_gnoll_m` rig tinted dapper vest/hat colors (dark green + brass), zero new generation -- the hats-off violence tell is staged HERE, at content time (marker's two text_variants), not at art/sprite time.
entities.observe: A Gnoll in a vest cut sharper than his manners need to be, tall hat squared like it's holding a rank. He watches the room's exits before he watches you.
entities.friendly_line: He inclines the hat half an inch — a genuine courtesy, not a performance of one. "A pleasure," he says, and seems to mean it.
talk_pool: Evening. Might I say, sir, you carry yourself like a person things happen to. We collect a few of those.
Manners cost nothing and buy everything, in my experience. Mind the rug — Normen fusses over it more than he'll admit.
You'll notice the hat stays on. Best we keep it that way, between friends.
We don't steal, whatever you've heard. We RECOVER. It's a finer distinction than it sounds, and it's the whole of our business.

dialogue.speaker: Wilovan
dialogue.text: Evening, sir. Fine weather for good behavior.

entities._comment_tint: Lifted to [0.75,0.8,0.68] -- as the marquee NPC, Wilovan must read clearly against the parlor's warm low-light grade; tint multiplies the rig, so low channel values darken him more than ambient decor. Keeps the dark-green dapper-vest identity (channel ratios preserved), just materially brighter.

entities._comment: THE BED RULE (standing, plan's user-ratified shape 3): the parlor's guest couch, sleep:true, unconditional once the parlor is reachable (no quest gate -- reaching this room already required the door chain: portal -> boulevard -> alleys door -> parlor door, no shortcut exists). #49: swapped from the reused `bed` sprite (a literal bed graphic, wrong read for a 'couch') to `bench` (assets/sprites/bench/Idle-Sheet.png, ALREADY committed + used once in runners_guild -- a real seating-furniture read, not a bed). Bbox math: 64x64 native @ render_scale 0.5 = 32x32px = 2.0x2.0 cells, anchor [0.4922,0.6875] (bottom-center-ish, CELL=16 convention). Placed at (2,7): horizontally spans the right half of col1 through the left half of col3 (bleeds into (1,7)/(3,7), both bare floor -- (3,7) is the player's own pre-bump standing cell, so the couch's armrest edge reads as the player standing right up against it, not clipping through anything solid); vertically spans the bottom ~37% of row6 through the top ~62% of row8 (also bare floor, no neighbor decor at (2,6)/(2,8)). Windowed-verified (peek screenshot): reads as an actual couch, no clipping through walls/other props.
entities.sleep_toast: Even a couch here fits like it was fitted for you. The Brothers do nothing halfway, not even hospitality.
